chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Ri'ab from Abu Basir from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who has a Christian wife, is it permissible for him to marry a Jewess upon her? He said: 'Indeed, the People of the Book are slaves of the Imam, and that is expanded for you by us, so there is no harm in him marrying.'
I said: 'He marries a slave girl upon her.' He said: 'It is not suitable for him to marry three slave girls.'

If he marries a free Muslim woman upon her, and she did not know that he has a Christian or Jewish wife, then he consummates the marriage with her, then she has what she took of the dowry. And if she wishes to remain with him afterwards, she remains; and if she wishes to go to her family, she goes.
When she has had three menstrual periods, or three months have passed for her, she becomes permissible for husbands.
I said: 'If he divorces the Jewess and the Christian woman before the waiting period of the Muslim woman ends, is there a way for him to return her to his house?' He said: 'Yes.'

key_terms.أَهْلُ الْكِتَابِ: People of the Book (Christians and Jews)
key_terms.عِدَّةُ الْمُسْلِمَةِ: The waiting period of the Muslim woman
key_terms.مَمَالِيُ لِلْإِمَامِ: Slaves of the Imam (subject to his discretion in marriage)

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia ruling on a man marrying a Jewish or Christian woman while already married to a Christian woman?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) rules that a man may marry a Jewish or Christian woman upon his existing Christian wife, as the People of the Book are considered 'slaves of the Imam' (under his discretion). The text further details the rights of the first wife if a free Muslim woman is married upon her, including her right to keep the dowry and choose to stay or leave, and clarifies the waiting period (iddah) and the husband's right to return the new wife if he divorces the others before the Muslim woman's iddah concludes.
